questions.q: What are the four habit‑tendency types identified in the book?
questions.why: The overview explains the habit tendency framework with those four types.

questions.q: Which type responds well to inner expectations but not to outer ones?
questions.why: Questioners are described as responding to inner expectations but resisting outer ones.

questions.q: What strategy does the book suggest to make a good habit easier to start?
a: Place the needed item in a visible spot, like shoes in the hallway
Set a strict deadline for the habit
Hire a personal trainer for accountability
Eliminate all other activities for the day
questions.why: The summary advises making good habits easy, e.g., leaving running shoes in the hallway.

questions.q: How does “temptation bundling” work according to the summary?
a: Pair an enjoyable activity with a habit you want to do
Reward yourself after completing the habit
Avoid the habit entirely until you feel ready
Replace the habit with a similar one
questions.why: Temptation bundling pairs joys (audiobooks) with struggles (gym) to boost habit adherence.

questions.q: What major life change does research cited in the book say can help create new habits?
a: A recent move, such as changing residence or family status
questions.why: Wendy Wood’s study found that participants who moved were more successful at improving diet.
